description: A Zed editor extension that adds rich language support for the Ren'Py visual-novel scripting language, aiming for feature parity with the official VSCode 'language-renpy' extension. Rich features (completion, hover, signature help, go-to-definition, references, document symbols, diagnostics, document color) are provided by a Rust language server built on the tower-lsp library. The Zed-facing extension is a WASM crate using zed_extension_api that registers the language, ships tree-sitter highlighting queries, and spawns the language server binary. Must be loadable as a Zed dev extension.

packages.name: zed-renpy-extension (root WASM crate)
packages.description: Zed extension entry point. Implements zed_extension_api::Extension to declare the Ren'Py language server command and locate/spawn the language-server binary. Ships extension.toml, languages/renpy/ config + tree-sitter queries, snippets.

packages.name: renpy-language-server
packages.description: Native Rust binary language server using tower-lsp. Implements LSP requests (textDocument/completion, hover, signatureHelp, definition, references, documentSymbol, publishDiagnostics, documentColor). Ports parsing/tokenizer + navigation-data logic from the VSCode extension.

dependencyChain: renpy-language-server (LSP binary) is independent and built first
zed-renpy-extension (WASM crate) references/locates the built LSP binary
crossPackageTriggers: Changing the LSP binary name, CLI args, or startup behavior requires updating the extension's language_server_command in the WASM crate.
Adding a new LSP capability in the server may require adjusting language config / capabilities advertised, and may need new tree-sitter queries for highlighting.
Changing the language id, file extensions, or grammar in extension.toml/languages config must stay in sync with the server's document selector assumptions.
notes: Greenfield project; not a Brazil workspace (no src/<Package>/Config files). project.json authored directly by the orchestrator to reflect the planned architecture. Use the tower-lsp library (https://github.com/ebkalderon/tower-lsp) for the Rust LSP implementation.
